summary: Aureth emerged from the first doubt as the embodiment of possibility. She is the Old God's daughter in a metaphysical sense: formed from his own uncertainty, but possessing an identity and purpose of her own.

name: Before the First Doubt
summary: In the oldest version of creation, the Old God of Fate existed alone. Fate was not merely a being who predicted events. Fate was the principle that events could happen only one way.
details: In the oldest version of creation, the Old God of Fate existed alone. Fate was not merely a being who predicted events. Fate was the principle that events could happen only one way. There was no uncertainty because nothing had ever departed from the intended pattern. Choice may have appeared to exist, but every choice had only one final answer. Possibility had not yet become an independent force. The Old God understood reality as a complete design rather than an unfolding story. Before doubt, the future was not unknown. It was simply waiting to arrive.

name: Intended Endgame — Integration Rather Than Defeat
summary: The preferred ending is not the destruction of the Old God of Fate. Destroying Fate entirely could leave reality unable to hold consequence, continuity, or meaning. Likewise, eliminating doubt would remove genuine choice.

name: The Dream Plane and Moon-Walking
summary: The Dream Plane is a shifting borderland connected to the Ethereal Realm. It is made from sleeping minds, remembered places, fears, hopes, and futures that have not yet become real. Unlike ordinary prophecy, the Dream Plane does not show what will happen. It shows what may happen, what once almost happened, and what a person believes might happen.

name: The First Doubt
summary: At some unknowable moment, the Old God of Fate experienced the first doubt. This was not a minor hesitation. It was the first event that Fate had not fully contained within certainty.
details: At some unknowable moment, the Old God of Fate experienced the first doubt. This was not a minor hesitation. It was the first event that Fate had not fully contained within certainty. The doubt created a crack within Fate's own mind or divine nature. That crack was the first space in which more than one future could exist. The existence of doubt did not destroy Fate, but it made Fate incomplete. From that internal fracture, possibility became capable of taking form. name: The Old God's Restoration
summary: The Old God of Fate is not necessarily seeking simple conquest. The restoration effort is driven by a belief that reality has become dangerously fragmented by uncertainty.
details: The Old God of Fate is not necessarily seeking simple conquest. The restoration effort is driven by a belief that reality has become dangerously fragmented by uncertainty. Permanent Dark Arcs reconnect reality through fixed points. Agents create certainty by removing, narrowing, or controlling choice. The Old God's servants may believe they are healing the world. Their methods become oppressive because they treat uncertainty as a wound rather than a necessary part of existence. name: The Origin and Nature of Magic
summary: Magic exists because Aureth discovered the spaces where fate could bend. A spell does not need to shatter destiny. It creates a temporary path through which another outcome can become real.
details: Magic exists because Aureth discovered the spaces where fate could bend. A spell does not need to shatter destiny. It creates a temporary path through which another outcome can become real. Divination explores futures that have not yet hardened into certainty. Transformation allows a creature to occupy a different possible form.
